question: HOw does the method perform compared with baselines?

answer.free_form_answer: On the datasets DE-EN, JA-EN, RO-EN, and EN-DE, the baseline achieves 29.79, 21.57, 32.70, and 26.02  BLEU score, respectively. The 1.5-entmax achieves  29.83, 22.13, 33.10, and 25.89 BLEU score, which is a difference of +0.04, +0.56, +0.40, and -0.13 BLEU score versus the baseline. The α-entmax achieves 29.90, 21.74, 32.89, and 26.93 BLEU score, which is a difference of +0.11, +0.17, +0.19, +0.91 BLEU score versus the baseline.

title: Adaptively Sparse Transformers

evidence: In particular, we analyzed how the attention heads in the proposed adaptively sparse Transformer can specialize more and with higher confidence. Our adaptivity strategy relies only on gradient-based optimization, side-stepping costly per-head hyper-parameter searches. Further speed-ups are possible by leveraging more parallelism in the bisection algorithm for computing $\alpha $-entmax.

title: Adaptively Sparse Transformers
answer_short: by replacing softmax with α-entmax, allowing low-scoring words to receive precisely zero weight, and enabling heads to choose between focused or spread-out behavior
answer_rationale: The model improves interpretability by replacing softmax with α-entmax, which allows low-scoring words to receive exactly zero weight, thereby reducing noise and enhancing focus. This sparsity enables attention heads to exhibit diverse behaviors, which helps uncover different head specializations without sacrificing accuracy. The adaptively sparse Transformer, as described in Text 1, explicitly improves interpretability compared to softmax Transformers by allowing context-dependent sparsity patterns and enabling heads to learn different sparsity preferences.
